samples.summary: `--dry-run` bypasses the new `seg()` segment guard, so the previewed URL is no longer the request that would be sent
samples.evidence: `printDryRun` builds `${server}/api/v1/workspaces/${config.workspace}${path}` with raw interpolation (packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts:13), and every dry-run call site interpolates ids raw as well — e.g. packages/cli/src/commands/cells.ts:55 `/documents/${docId}/tabs/${tab}/cells/${ref}`, packages/cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:72, packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:152/188, packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:63, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:146, packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:140, packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-import.ts:84. Since the diff made the real client encode every id via `seg()` (http-client.ts:71), the two now disagree: `wafflebase docs delete '../../x' --dry-run` prints a traversal URL that the real request would encode, and `--dry-run` happily previews a `.`/`..` id that the real path now refuses with `Invalid path segment`. docs/design/cli.md:811 states `--dry-run` "validates inputs, resolves the target API endpoint, and prints the request that would be sent". Fix belongs in dry-run.ts (or by routing the preview through the same segment helper).

samples.summary: `login` still reports backend HTTP failures as bare prose + `process.exit(1)`, diverging from the now-uniform error-envelope contract the diff and docs assert
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62/79/96 print prose (`Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP ${wsRes.status})`) and call `process.exit(1)` without the `{error:{code,message}}` envelope, while docs/design/cli.md:1064-1078 (updated by this change) now states every backend failure surfaces `HTTP_ERROR` or `SESSION_EXPIRED` and packages/cli/README.md:116-128 says the same. The task file docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-upstream-error-envelope-todo.md:82 declares login's workspace fetch an explicit non-goal, so this may be intentional — but the generalized docs now over-claim for this command.

samples.summary: `UpstreamHttpError` is exported but referenced nowhere outside the file that defines it
samples.evidence: Repo-wide grep for `UpstreamHttpError` matches only packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:187/194/214/229 and the task doc; no test or other module imports it (the new packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts imports only `forwardUpstreamError`, `outputError`, `upstreamErrorJson`). knip's unused-exports lane runs on this repo, so either make it non-exported or assert on it from a consumer.

samples.summary: `files download` can now emit `HTTP_ERROR: "HTTP 200"` on the ok-but-no-bytes branch
samples.evidence: packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:56 guards `!res.ok || !res.bytes` and then calls `upstreamErrorJson(res)`, which formats `HTTP ${res.status}`. On the second disjunct `res.status` is a success status, so the envelope reads `{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}` — previously that branch printed the bare `{error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}`. Reachability depends on `downloadFileDocument` ever returning ok with no bytes (http-client.ts:309 always sets them), so this may be dead, but the message is misleading if it is not.
